Discover the story of humanity — past and present. At Brandeis University, Anthropology students don’t just study cultures, they experience them through hands-on exploration and interdisciplinary learning. By exploring multiple anthropological disciplines, students gain the tools to uncover the richness of civilizations that shaped our world.

“By understanding who we are as people, you can really change the way you see modern culture, the world, and how people behave,” says Assistant Professor of Anthropology Charlotte Goudge.

From excavating model archaeological sites to studying how ancient communities interacted with their environments, Brandeis anthropology majors graduate prepared to make meaningful connections between the past and present, bringing a deeper understanding to the world we share.

****
Video description: Assistant Professor of Anthropology Charlotte Goudge and undergraduate student Oles Tymofeichuk discuss the importance of anthropology and what it entails. Footage shows Tymofeichuk and other students excavating a model maritime archaeological site and interviews of both les Tymofeichuk and Professor Goudge.

From rural Maine to Brandeis, Elizabeth Ford ’27 is helping her community find connection and hope through Pride.

Noam Reiner ’27, a computer science and math double-major, had an idea that a summer internship at Capital One in McLean, Virginia, might give her valuable insights into how to turn her academic interests into an absorbing career.

caption:
What does it mean to study Physics & Biophysics at Brandeis? For our first Major Mondays Series, meet Elena Amado ’25, who’s exploring both fields.

From exploring the building blocks of the universe to diving into interdisciplinary science, Elena shares why studying at Brandeis is so unique.

“We’re an R1 school, but we’re a very small R1 school, and that gives you a lot of attention from professors and from a lot of people in the community that you otherwise wouldn’t at a larger research university.”

Big opportunities. Personal attention. Endless possibilities.

****

****

Vivienne Raczkowski ’26 spent the summer studying pollinators across Yellowstone, Grand Teton and Glacier National Parks as part of a FIELDS Fellowship to examine the impacts of climate change.

Raczkowski took part in the fellowship at the encouragement of environmental studies professor Colleen Hitchcock, who also briefly joined the expedition.

Graduate school is on Raczkowski’s horizon as well, though she hopes to gain more field experience before pursuing a master’s or PhD.

caption:
Today we commemorate the tragic events of September 11, 2001. We remember.

The Brandeis University Peace Monument is located in the circular seating area between Usdan and Pearlman. In the very center of the monument is a beautiful mosaic of a dove — the international symbol of peace. Encircling the mosaic are tiles engraved with the word "peace" in 40 of the languages that community members speak at Brandeis.

Today is Fresh Check Day!

Fresh Check Day, the signature program of the Jordan Porco Foundation, is an uplifting mental health promotion and suicide prevention event for colleges that includes interactive expo booths, peer-to-peer messaging, support of multiple campus departments and groups, free food, entertainment, prizes and giveaways.

The event is supported by various campus partners including @brandeiswellness, @brandeisacserv, @bemcobrandeis, @brandeisjudges, @brandeis_dse, @brandeiscommunityliving, @spirituallifebrandeis, @hiattcareercenter, @brandeis_sas, @brandeis_gsc, @brandeisuniversitysu and more.

In an era defined by rapidly changing careers, evolving student needs, and technological transformation, liberal arts education faces a vital question: how can it remain both meaningful and relevant?

On Wednesday, September 10, 2025, Brandeis University convenes a thoughtful, inclusive conversation with leading educators, policymakers, and innovators at the National Press Club (@pressclubdc) in Washington, D.C. Together, they’ll explore how institutions can better prepare students to thrive in the real world.

Learn more about the Brandeis Plan 🔗 in bio.

caption:
Brandeis University President Arthur Levine outlined The Brandeis Plan to Reinvent the Liberal Arts during a forum with higher education and policy leaders at the National Press Club in Washington, D.C. on September 10.

The plan is backed by faculty and supported with a $25 million investment from the Brandeis Board of Trustees to expand internships and career pathways, support faculty in redesigning programs and degrees, and launch the Center for Careers and Applied Liberal Arts. It will infuse career readiness into every aspect of the student experience, Levine explained.

Learn more at 🔗 in bio.

caption:
Katriona is a Biology (@biobrandeis) and Environmental Studies (@brandeisenvironmentalstudies) double major and captain of the Brandeis Cross Country team (@brandeisxctf). She loves exploring the overlap between her fields—whether that’s studying trees, learning how climate impacts ecosystems, or looking at science with a holistic perspective.

“Taking classes that overlap between my Biology and Environmental Studies majors, like Biology of Climate Change, has helped me understand the fluid nature of science and attack every problem from an interdisciplinary lens. ” – Katriona Briggs ’26

When she’s not in class or leading her team, you might find her creating art in the pottery studio or enjoying the view from the SCC balcony at dusk. 💙
